# Find and fix code hygiene problems safely

Use this skill to identify dead code, commented-out code and recurring anti-patterns, then plan or execute cleanup without turning hygiene into risky churn.

## When to use it

Use `code-hygiene review` to measure the backlog. Use `code-hygiene fix` only after the backlog and phases are approved. It is not a license to refactor unrelated code during a feature.

## What you need

Bring the scope and mode: `review` or `fix`. For `fix`, bring the approved backlog items and acceptance checks.

## Try it

Slash-command harnesses:

```text
/code-hygiene review HarborTasks export and reporting code. Measure dead code,
commented-out blocks and anti-patterns; do not modify source.
```

Codex equivalent:

```text
$code-hygiene review HarborTasks export and reporting code.
```

## What happens

Review mode inventories hygiene issues, classifies them and writes a measured backlog. Fix mode builds a phased, test-guarded remediation plan and applies approved phases as small, labelled changes.

## What you get

Illustrative artifact shape:

```text
docs/hygiene/backlog.md
  class, location, lines, percentage, evidence
docs/hygiene/remediation-plan.md
  phase, files, checks, rollback note
```

## Review before continuing

Check whether each finding is real, whether intentional markers were excluded, and whether fixes are tied to tests. Do not approve broad cleanup that makes a feature harder to review.

## Tips and recovery

If review finds unrelated problems during another task, capture them as backlog rather than fixing immediately. If a cleanup phase fails tests, revert that phase rather than continuing through more files.

## Where to go next

Use [implement](#skill-implement) for approved repair phases, or [forensicreview](#skill-forensicreview) if hygiene is one part of a broader repository review.
